title: Split the Array
summary: Given an integer array of even length, determine if it can be divided into two arrays of equal length, each containing distinct elements.
statement: Given an integer array of even length, determine if it can be divided into two arrays of equal length, each containing distinct elements.
constraints: Split an even-length array into two arrays of equal length.
Each result must contain distinct values internally.
Return whether such a split exists; original order need not be preserved.
hints: A value can appear at most once in each of the two result arrays.
Therefore any frequency above two is impossible.
If all frequencies are at most two, put duplicate copies on opposite sides and balance singleton values.
The two equal-sized halves have total capacity n and duplicates consume one slot per side, so remaining singleton slots balance.
editorial: The two equal-sized halves have total capacity n and duplicates consume one slot per side, so remaining singleton slots balance.

tests.explanation: Place one copy of repeated values one and two in each half, then distribute three and four.
Four copies of one cannot fit into two halves without repetition.
